newsitem.title: USA: Wolfensohn - World Bank ready to support Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: Wolfensohn - World Bank ready to support Bulgaria.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn lauded Bulgarian plans to adopt a currency board and pledged support for the country on Friday.
"We stand ready to enter in support of Bulgaria," Wolfensohn told reporters at a news conference held in conjunction with the World Bank/IMF spring meetings.
"One of the preconditions that I think was suggested by the Fund was in fact the currency board and I am delighted that it is in fact forthcoming," Wolfensohn added.

Under a $548 million, 20-month standby agreement sealed with the IMF earlier this month, Bulgaria pledged to introduce in June a self-regulating restrictive monetary mechanism, known as the currency board, aimed at restoring confidence in the country's shaky financial system.

Under the currency board system, the Bulgarian lev will be pegged to an anchor currency at a rate that cannot be adjusted. The amount of levs in circulation must be matched precisely by the amount of foreign exchange reserves under this system.
